data.description: The UN General Assembly on Friday voted to shift away from the 16th-century Mercator map, designed by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator, for a more accurate one reflecting the true size of continents. data.title: 'Italian opposition fragmented: No alternative leader, no other possible leader than Giorgia Meloni'
data.description: Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Political analyst Lorenzo Pregliasco, co-founder of polling agency YouTrend and adjunct professor at the University of Bologna. He argues that Giorgia Meloni’s unusual longevity in office is best understood not simply as a record of political strength, but as the product of a carefully calibrated governing strategy. Meloni has maintained stability partly by avoiding structural reforms disruptive enough to mobilize multiple constituencies against her at once. Her dominance within Fratelli d’Italia, the absence of a credible alternative leader, and a fragmented opposition have reinforced that advantage.

data.title: Losing a parent is a bewildering, lonely experience. Here are the things I wish I had known before | Gaby Hinsliff
data.description: There’ll be exhaustion, love tinged with occasional rage, even moments of black humour. But my mum would want me to tell you: don’t be afraid My mother’s house looks exactly as she left it. Two novels sit by the armchair, their pages neatly marked for book group. Pinned to the noticeboard is a shopping list in only slightly shaky writing, with “FRUIT!” in urgent capitals, and “make soup” underlined. The sole outward signs of something missing are her cats twining needily around me – loneliness having finally overcome their innate horror of visitors – and the one thing I can’t bear to look at, which is the empty hospital bed marooned bleakly in the sitting room. Delivered by social services when it was deemed she could no longer manage stairs, it is now stripped bare, awaiting collection. Another family will be needing it. Have a baby and the world falls over itself to offer advice. But losing a parent remains a private, bewildering, lonely affair Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The unsettling rise of cat seducers: ‘My little companion was missing – and I was consumed with anger’
data.description: Has your cat been gaining weight and staying out at night, only to arrive home reeking of marijuana? These are just some of the signs that a neighbour is trying to entice them away ... When Amy’s cat, Sid*, first started spending more time away from home, Amy* put it down to wanderlust. A former street cat, Sid had landed on his feet in her leafy London suburb, but still retained his free-roaming sociability. When Sid began disappearing for up to days at a time though, Amy worried. She put a tracker on his collar to find out where he was going. She didn’t expect to discover him a few doors up the road. Sid is roaming – but most of the time, for entire afternoons and even sometimes overnight, he is with Amy’s neighbour. “He is in her house, constantly, all the time,” she says. This is not a coincidence. Sid might not be getting six dinners, like his famous namesake in Inga Moore ’s 1990 children’s book, but the neighbour is certainly spoiling him, as she recently let slip to Amy’s partner. “She’s feeding him organic chicken!” Amy says indignantly. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Then who or what did we cremate?’ Daughter’s horror at finding bones in British wildfire victims’ car
data.description: Danielle Gillam-Kirton claims police botched investigation into her parents’ deaths in Spain and is demanding answers When Danielle Gillam-Kirton’s parents, Pete and Fran Gillam, were killed in July’s Spanish wildfires, she felt her nightmare could get no worse. The much-loved couple had built their home in Bédar in Almería after retirement, becoming part of a tight-knit community. Fran, a former headteacher, loved to organise quiz nights to raise money for the local school and the couple enjoyed playing padel at a nearby sports club. Spanish police told Gillam-Kirton that the vehicle in which her parents died had been “inspected meticulously” and no possessions had been found. But Gillam-Kirton, an assistant headteacher from Nottinghamshire, was sure her parents must have been wearing their wedding rings when they died. Continue reading...

data.title: Death on the road to Rafah: the night the IDF targeted World Central Kitchen aid workers
data.description: The Israeli army had helped plan the delivery of food aid on 1 April 2024, but things went wrong from the beginning and ended in seven deaths • Exclusive: why seven international aid workers were killed in Israeli airstrike On the evening of 1 April 2024, a team of aid workers from World Central Kitchen (WCK) stood on Gaza’s Mediterranean shore overseeing the unloading of a barge full of desperately needed food on a makeshift jetty made of sand and rubble. The Gaza war had been raging for six months and Israel’s closure of land crossings had left the whole territory facing the threat of famine. WCK and local Palestinian contractors had constructed the jetty out of everything they could lay their hands on, including debris from the bombed house of one of the contractors, so that the pallets of humanitarian assistance could be delivered by boat from Cyprus. data.title: ‘Guilt by association’: why seven international aid workers were killed in Israeli airstrike
data.description: Exclusive: Guardian investigation reveals targeting of World Central Kitchen convoy was result of widely used military tactic • Death on the road to Rafah: the night the IDF targeted World Central Kitchen aid workers Seven aid workers killed in an airstrike in Gaza were marked as targets under an Israeli military practice of establishing guilt by association, a Guardian investigation shows. A top Israeli military prosecutor announced last month that he would not pursue criminal proceedings for the April 2024 incident in which drones fired missiles at three clearly marked World Central Kitchen (WCK) cars soon after they had escorted a food aid delivery to Gaza. Three British humanitarian workers along with an Australian, a Palestinian, a Pole and a dual US-Canadian national were killed. Continue reading...

All eyes are on Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, where about 1.7 million people are eligible to vote, followed by Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin on 20 September. In all three contests, the far-right, anti-immigrant Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) is expected to make strong gains. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘We’re plausibly close to crossing the line’: are warnings of uncontrollable AI coming true?
data.description: A spate of serious safety incidents have increased fears about the power and impenetrability of the most advanced models Picture humanity in a boat being swept down a raging river, praying there is no Niagara Falls ahead. Or imagine standing with the pioneering physicists in 1942 before they triggered the first self-sustaining nuclear fission chain reaction beneath a Chicago stadium. These were two of the analogies used this week by Prof Robert Trager, an expert in the nascent field of AI governance, to describe the perilous but potential-filled moment the world stands at with accelerating artificial intelligence. data.title: ‘There is light at the end of this tunnel. But the tunnel is filled with sewage’: Marina Hyde on finding hope in political chaos
data.description: It’s been an era of global instability, complete with ejector-seat prime ministers, Mars-bound baddies and even a celebrity ski-massacre trial … • How posh are you? Do you have a therapist? What would you say to Trump at a party? Marina Hyde answers readers’ questions Let me kick off by letting a little daylight in on magic. If you’ve got a book out in September, you’re probably sending the publisher the final version of the introduction four months earlier. So I guess the moment I truly knew that Keir Starmer was finished was the moment, in the first days of May, when I typed the words “we’ve had three prime ministers since my last book”. At that point it became an absolute cast-iron cosmic inevitability that we would have had yet another prime minister by the time the book was out. Nailed on. It’s the equivalent of lighting a cigarette so the bus turns up immediately. So, four prime ministers in four years … Good times, possibly, for someone whose job involves writing about prime ministers. But not good times for Britain, or indeed for the seemingly endless series of outgoing premiers. Being British prime minister has become the biggest ejector-seat job since the noughties, when the US would announce they’d killed “the al-Qaida No 3” about twice a month. Continue reading...

data.title: Tender Loving Care review – Mike Leigh’s tender and elusive study of love and mortality
data.description: Telluride film festival Alice Bailey Johnson and Kate O’Flynn lead a complicated, quietly heartbreaking drama about friendship, ageing parents and the sadness of lives moving inexorably on Mike Leigh’s new film – perhaps his last – is a poignant, intergenerational drama of happy-sad acceptance that life goes on, until it doesn’t go on. And then you have to come to terms with the mortality of your elderly parents and by that same token, with the end that is waiting for you too. The decency and clarity of the film are a tonic. It is a movie with one of Leigh’s overtly positive and even sugary titles, like Life Is Sweet (1990) or Happy-Go-Lucky (2008), as distinct from his darker ones: Secrets & Lies (1996) or Hard Truths (2024). But his sweet titles are not simply satirical and intended to mean the opposite: it is more complicated and elusive, and even the contrast here between the two heroines’ private and professional lives isn’t straightforwardly a matter of irony. As so often, the dialogue has that unique Leigh cartoonish quality that isn’t caricature, and the characters often speak with an almost wartime chirpiness in a world of peckers kept up and noses kept clean. This is a perkiness that the thirtysomethings have unexpectedly inherited and modified from their old mum and dad, and Leigh leaves it to the audience to judge the consequent tone of the drama and the appropriate tone of their response. Continue reading...

data.title: 50? Moi? How The Muppets rocked the world with anarchy, nonsense and the inimitable Miss Piggy
data.description: Half a century on, Jim Henson’s fuzzy felt friends are as influential as Monty Python and the Beatles. It’s been a wild journey of  nightclubbing, light operas, duetting with Debbie Harry and tying John Cleese to a chair Fifty years ago today, it was time to play the music and time to light the lights. On 5 September 1976, the British public first met the Muppets – an epochal moment in the history of light entertainment whose reverberations are still felt to this day. This was the show that saw Rita Moreno conclude a performance of Fever by smashing a puppet’s head between two cymbals, Alice Cooper convince the characters to sell their souls to the devil and Vincent Price cover Carole King’s You’ve Got a Friend, accompanied by ghosts. The Muppet Show was not like other television programmes. Continue reading...

data.title: A city break in Łódź, Poland’s capital of cinema and factories
data.description: The imposing red-brick mills of its industrial past are a stunning example of urban regeneration in the former ‘city of a thousand chimneys’ Sometimes travel delivers a real shock. I’m moving along the boulevards in the Polish city of Łódź, enjoying the excellent cafes and warm sunshine, when I spot the vans. They are parked up on the verge, with racks of clothing and heavily laden tables behind. I can’t resist a Sunday morning market and walk towards a group of men huddled around a car that is covered in blankets. And then it happens. They turn – and I see they are weighing pistols in their hands. I recognise the lean profile of a German Luger, and then the bulkier Colt 45. There is a second of doubt. I hesitate. They replace the weapons on the display and walk away laughing. I approach. On the car roof is a row of dusty soldiers’ helmets. “We were repairing a pavement in the centre of town,” says the seller cheerfully, handing me a badge to inspect. “Imagine! For 80 years, all this stuff was just under our feet.” Continue reading...

data.title: Colin from Accounts: a show so fearless and hilarious that I want to get a tattoo of it
data.description: It’s deliciously satirical, fizzes with electric chemistry – and it’s snortingly funny too. If you haven’t watched the worst named show on TV yet, do so. Right now! Sometimes the best things in life have the worst names. The Beatles. Smeg fridges. Nintendo Wii. But top of the tree is Colin from Accounts (Monday 7 September, 10pm, BBC Two), a name so bland I almost slipped into medical unconsciousness upon hearing it. It’s worse than bland. There’s an aspect of comedy-tie zaniness to it, a “Look, we’re calling our possibly office-based sitcom the most boring thing we can think of!” tedium. One can imagine the lazy jokes, the stock characters. Within 15 minutes of watching it, I was genuinely toying with the idea of a CFA tattoo. How did this unpromising Australian import become my favourite? By being a showcase for fearless writing, electric chemistry and delicious comic timing. Written by real-life partners Patrick Brammall and Harriet Dyer , it tracks the relationship of medical student Ashley and Gordon, a brewery owner and ball cancer survivor. The romance, like their writing, is allergic to schmaltz. Their meet-cute occurs in the street when Ashley flashes a boob at Gordon, causing him to crash his car and permanently disable a stray dog that they unwillingly adopt together. (That’s Colin. It’s not really about Colin.) Continue reading...

data.title: Why the Bayeux tapestry and Franco-British relations are natural bedfellows
data.description: Tapestry’s loan to UK is just another chapter in the love-hate relationship that has spanned the centuries since it was created Five British prime ministers ago – and six French ones – when Emmanuel Macron first confirmed that France would return the Bayeux tapestry to Britain after 1,000 years, he told an audience at Sandhurst and Theresa May – the No 10 seat-warmer of the day – that when it came to France and Britain there were “two things that nothing can change, be it a vote or a political decision: our history and our geography”. It was January 2018, 18 months after the UK had voted to leave the EU, and relations between the near neighbours were not good. The French political establishment had been shocked and angered by Brexit; personal relations were frazzled, and cross-Channel government contacts measurably dwindling . This was not a rupture that a piece of embroidered medieval linen, however perfectly it represented that tangled history, was going to solve on its own. Continue reading...

data.title: Kimi Antonelli: ‘The F1 environment is great but at times it can be very brutal’
data.description: Before his home grand prix, the Mercedes driver opens up on his rocky debut season and quest to become the first Italian world champion since 1953 If Kimi Antonelli feels any pressure as the favourite to take the Formula One world championship at just 20 years old and in his second year in the sport, it is imperceptible. He admits F1 can be brutal but a thing of beauty too, a labour of love for the Italian who has been a revelation this season. Compelling and brilliant, that he is also endearing and likable marks Antonelli out as more than just a potential champion. Sitting in the Mercedes motorhome it is impossible not to be struck by how young he looks, the tousled hair, engaging smile and eyes gleaming with youthful enthusiasm. He speaks with an open candour, the air of a kid in a sweetshop who still can’t quite believe all those sherbet lemons are there for the taking. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The noise was unbelievable’: the referee’s view of Mexico v England at the World Cup
data.description: England’s manager Thomas Tuchel called the officiating ‘just not good enough’ in the fiery last-16 tie. Now Alireza Faghani gives his version of events It was 6pm on 5 July in Mexico City, and Alireza Faghani, a 48-year-old Australian-Iranian, was asleep in the locker room, snoring. His assistants had turned the music down. Had it not been for the muffled roar of nearly 90,000 fans through the concrete walls of the Estadio Azteca, he could have slept until the following morning. Faghani was the referee for Mexico v England in the last 16 at the 2026 World Cup. Mexico hadn’t lost a competitive game at the Azteca since 2013, at least in part because they’re used to the conditions. Situated 2,240 metres above sea level, the air contains less oxygen. Opponents struggle to breathe, let alone win. Continue reading...

data.title: Booyakasha! Ali G is back – but even he can't match the absurdity of modern Britain | Jason Okundaye
data.description: Sacha Baron Cohen’s character once exposed the contradictions of an emerging multicultural nation. But nearly 30 years on Britain has changed – and so has the joke And so the nostalgia machine grinds on, dragging another pop culture corpse back into the light: yes, it’s the return of Ali G. Respeck. Sacha Baron Cohen’s skull-cap-wearing, “rudebwoy” wankster is staging a comeback with Ali G: Who Iz I?. The new film, premiering next month, is a mockumentary that sees the character starting a family with long-term companion Julie (thinking his approach to fatherhood will be “absent”) and embracing TikTok, all while donning new fake dreads and a rastacap. Jason Okundaye is an assistant Opinion editor at the Guardian Continue reading...

But nearly 30 years on Britain has changed – and so has the joke And so the nostalgia machine grinds on, dragging another pop culture corpse back into the light: yes, it’s the return of Ali G. Respeck. Sacha Baron Cohen’s skull-cap-wearing, “rudebwoy” wankster is staging a comeback with Ali G: Who Iz I?. The new film, premiering next month, is a mockumentary that sees the character starting a family with long-term companion Julie (thinking his approach to fatherhood will be “absent”) and embracing TikTok, all while donning new fake dreads and a rastacap. Jason Okundaye is an assistant Opinion editor at the Guardian Continue reading...

data.title: How much does Donald Trump care about winning the midterms? Apparently, not much at all | Jonathan Freedland
data.description: Such is the US president’s narcissism that he would see a Democratic victory as proof that he’s indispensable – meanwhile, his every decision spells calamity for voters What is Donald Trump playing at? If it’s true that the best way of understanding the behaviour of an organisation is to assume it’s controlled by a secret cabal of its enemies, perhaps that same logic extends to the current conduct of the president of the United States. Maybe he secretly wants Republicans to lose the looming midterm elections that will decide the balance of power in the US for the next two years and for which the first postal ballots were sent out today. That’s not as mad a theory as it sounds. Indeed, there are at least two reasons why Trump might either be unbothered by Republican defeat in November or even covertly desire it. We’ll come to those, but let’s start with a pattern of behaviour that is hard to explain as anything other than calculated self-sabotage. Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: The Trump White House’s fetish for gamer culture has moved up a level with new arcade
data.description: A string of distractions on the US government’s own website invite you to catch pixelated migrants – showing gaming’s potential to be nastily weaponised The Trump White House on Thursday released a horrible little propaganda arcade via its website, a collection of nasty riffs on popular games. Wrapped in the cutesy, nostalgic aesthetic of early-90s pixel art, these mindless fascist diversions are harmless-looking, but their intent is stomach-turning: this is the appropriation of play in service of propaganda. It’s just the latest in a series of attempts from Trump’s administration to use video game memes and imagery to further its messaging. Having riffed on Halo and Pokémon in social media ads last year, inviting potential ICE recruits to “stop the flood” and “catch ’em all”, this time the administration has ripped off a series of recognisable games. Flappy Bill, perhaps the least gross, is a version of the old mobile hit Flappy Bird, except here you’re an eagle with a scroll in its claws. Supply Line could almost be an educational game about healthy food in schools, where you sort junk food off a conveyor belt destined for school lunches, except for some reason you play as a boxer who becomes more bloodied with every seed-oil containing, ultra-processed food item that you fail to punch into the garbage chute. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Reform’s funding scandal: Nigel Farage has questions to answer | Editorial
data.description: An undercover investigation raises issues around foreign money, political transparency and the rightwing populist party’s fitness for power Reform UK’s conference was to open showcasing a party ready for government. It did so with two top aides removed after an investigation aired on Channel 4 , its finances under police scrutiny and seven in 10 voters, polls suggest, regarding its leader, Nigel Farage, as sleazy – double the number who thought the same of Andy Burnham. Reform, a rightwing populist party, says it will take power back from a corrupt establishment. The latest scandal raises a question: does Reform oppose the influence of big money – or just who benefits from it? Undercover reporters from Verbatim Investigations , founded by journalists from the US Center for Climate Reporting, pretended to be a wealthy American father and his UK-based son who wanted to donate to Reform. In the UK, foreign donations are banned from politics. But that allegedly was ignored. Verbatim’s team filmed their meetings with James Orr, a Cambridge academic specialising in ethics, and Reform’s head of policy, as well as with Dan Jukes, Mr Farage’s close aide. Both have been “ removed ” from their posts. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...

data.title: Iranian town mourns after deadly strike on wedding
data.description: Mourning turns to anger as residents of Kuhestak say Baloch communities are being placed in path of conflict People in Kuhestak, a predominantly Baloch city in Iran’s southern Hormozgan province, are mourning after a strike on a wedding killed at least four people, including a child, and injured more than 60, according to local authorities. The blast hit at around 9.30pm on 1 September, turning a night of celebration into one of devastation for the small coastal community, which is on the strait of Hormuz. Continue reading...

data.title: The Basics of Philosophy review – Paul Schrader back to his cool, cruel best
data.description: Venice film festival When a figure from his past turns up to a family funeral, a college professor faces an agonising dilemma that makes him question his own morality and whether he can change Paul Schrader is back with his most successful picture since First Reformed in 2018. It’s a stereotypical Schrader study of masculinity in some ways, about a man agonising over moral choice and ethical behaviour while – as so often in Schrader’s movies – reading and writing philosophy in an austerely furnished room. And yet there is nothing abstract about the issue he faces here. The film moves with a determined suspenseful tread, everything hangs together right up to the queasy final shot and Schrader flavours everything with a streak of melodrama and even a kind of gaunt black comedy. Karl Glusman’s cameo is surely the weirdest thing at Venice this year. The scene is a blandly prestigious liberal arts college, presided over by a genial, grey-haired dean, played in cameo by Richard Gere. John Jorrisen, played by Jack Huston, is the star of the philosophy faculty, enjoying agreeable mid-career success, working on a book about Spinoza. He is cordially resigned to bored students showing up to his “The Basics Of Philosophy” course for what they assume will be easy extra credit, attracted by that undemanding word “basic”. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Many of us in Israel live in a state of shock at the savagery’: veteran director Amos Gitai returns to Gaza
data.description: The writer-director once called Israel’s ‘one-man New Wave’ is in Venice with The Road to Jericho, a new and poetic attempt to highlight the plight of those in the occupied West Bank The Palestinian village of Khan al-Ahmar sits off dust-blown Highway-1, between Jerusalem and Jericho in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. At the village centre is the “school of tires”, a fragile construction of rubber, wood and adobe which is attended by around 300 Bedouin boys and girls. The Israeli authorities denied the villagers an official building permit and ruled that the entire settlement is illegal. For the past eight years the school has been operating under threat of imminent demolition, a symbol of resistance to widespread settler violence. It is only international pressure, says the veteran Israeli writer-director Amos Gitai, that has kept the place upright and still open. “The school has become a litmus paper. It is a test of how far the international community will go [to protect the rights of the people of Khan al-Ahmar]. For once, on this issue, Europe stood up and said no.” As for the future, who can tell? Continue reading...

data.title: A Long Winter review – hope, desire and subversion in Andrew Haigh’s beautiful winter western
data.description: Telluride film festival In a remote Colorado farmstead, a family with a mother gone missing finds a strange buoyancy and freedom as they wait for the snows to melt Andrew Haigh’s mysterious and beautiful new film is adapted by him from the 2006 story by Colm Tóibín , transplanting the action from the 1930s Spanish Pyrenees to the wintry, vertiginous landscapes of Colorado about the time of the Korean war. It is a poignant, subversive study of grief and desire, and the terrible, infantilised loneliness of men without women; it is fiercely acted, and wonderfully shot by cinematographer André Turpin. Lester, played by Ebon Moss-Bachrach, is a grizzled, hardened farmsteader in the remote hills whose family has a certain sufficiency from their livestock; he makes a precarious living breeding rabbits for their meat and fur. data.title: Katseye review – petulant hyperpop bops from a girl group in crisis
data.description: O2 Arena, London Fans scream ‘eat zucchini’ as if their lives depend on it as the six-piece’s remaining members strut their way through chest-rattling hits, ludicrous bangers and flaccid flops It takes a certain amount of resilience to be a Katseye fan. Since debuting three years ago via the boot camp meets reality TV show The Debut: Dream Academy, the multinational K-pop hybrid girl band have put their so-called Eyekons through the wringer . Last month alone they lost their second member to a “personal health and wellness” related hiatus, with Sophia joining Manon (who stepped away in more mysterious circumstances back in February) on the sidelines. Weeks later, they landed their first US No 1 album with Wild, a collection led by the carbonated dance-pop rocket Pinky Up – a song referred to by the band’s many online detractors as “skibidi toilet music” (ie slop). Even as this debut arena tour arrived in the UK, there were fears the newly reshaped quartet might be reduced to a trio after Megan sprained her ankle. But if the fans are worried, they don’t show it, their ear-piercing screams drowning out the opening Hootie Frutti , a sonic melange that somehow makes Brazilian funk sound leaden. By the time petulant hyperpop bop Internet Girl kicks in they’re screaming lines like “eat zucchini, eat zucchini” as if their lives depend on it. Continue reading...

data.title: Holly Throsby: ‘I was proud to not make a breakup album’
data.description: The writer and musician on returning to music, finding herself, and why right now is a terrifying time to be an artist Holly Throsby does not enjoy having her photo taken. There’s even a song on her new album about it. But you wouldn’t know it to see her gamely bush-bashing off the beaten track to pose in a cluster of supersized lomandra for the perfect portrait. After all, this is her happy place. Walking along various bush tracks is a daily ritual for Throsby. A sense of nature gently pervades her seventh album, Normal Magic. It is in the imagery of sparkling water and swims; gardens and birds; bushfires and wind and rain on the roof. The album itself feels like the breaking of a drought: her first solo record in nine years. In the intervening time, she moved to the New South Wales south coast, had her second child, wrote her third novel, and recorded and toured a second album with Seeker Lover Keeper, her collaborative project with Sarah Blasko and Sally Seltmann. She has hardly been idle. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Men calling us woke need our show more than most’: punks Piss on finding strength in visceral confrontations of sexual violence
data.description: The Vancouver band earned a cult fandom for their uncompromising gigs. As they ready their brutal debut album, they discuss subverting audience expectations and the nightly toll of excavating trauma onstage You’d be hard pressed to find a band with fewer airs and graces than Piss. First, there’s the unavoidable matter of their name, which they style in all caps, no nonsense; a word that scans as vulgar and combative but also somewhat facetious when displayed on their merch in loopy cursive, sometimes decorated with bows. The Vancouver quartet’s music is a merciless cyclone of hardcore, poetry, sound collage and performance art that revolves entirely around singer Taylor Zantingh’s experiences with sexual violence. On stage at Eindhoven’s Hit the City festival in late August, the band greets the stacked crowd with a trigger warning before drummer Garreth Roberts, bassist Gavin Moya and guitarist Tyler Paterson launch into pulverising fits of noise-punk, broken up by audio samples of children laughing and feminist writer Andrea Dworkin talking about pornography. Zantingh hurls herself around, clutching at her stomach and flinging her pigtails before winding down to a nervous, twitching standstill. The intense set is finely tuned to present a narrative of gender-based violence not as entertainment, but as lived experience. They play it exactly the same every night, and have done for the last two years. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Bold, brilliant, thrilling’: leading authors on the novels every school should teach
data.description: A new term, a new PM … time for a new English curriculum? We ask writers from Ben Okri to Samantha Harvey to pick books that will inspire a lifelong love of reading For the first time ever, we have a British prime minister who studied for an English degree. Not all of his 58 predecessors went to university, but those who did favoured subjects such as history and classics and, more recently, philosophy, politics and economics. Yet reading fiction is a fantastic preparation for life, for understanding people and the times through which we live. Novels encourage empathy, they help you to stand in other people’s shoes, to navigate complicated, sometimes conflicting emotions, they entertain and bring joy. The creative industries contribute some £145.8bn each year to the UK economy; it is our soft superpower. In other words, books matter. Reading matters. Continue reading...

data.title: The best recent poetry – review roundup
data.description: Fetch by Colin Bramwell;  Girling by Eve Esfandiari-Denney; The Dead One, The Unconscious One, Thundering in Your Ear, Thriving Slumber by Jay Gao; Belling the Leopard by Clementine Ewokolo Burnley; The Matter by Padraig Regan Fetch by Colin Bramwell ( And Other Stories, £14.99 ) Bramwell’s translation of Fernando Pessoa’s work into Scots won him considerable recognition: it took the Oxford Weidenfeld Translation prize and the Highland Book Prize. Between source and target language, there is always a gap; the translator endeavours within that gap to identify meaning and intention, and that is the difficult work of translation. Fetch, Bramwell’s own debut collection, lyrically thematises this gap in the poet-human’s condition: “I’m an instrument for something else / a digital piano that if you opened it up / you wouldn’t understand the wiring.” Fetch (in Celtic folklore, a doppelganger) is by turns solemnly tender, comically worldly, literarily devout. Here you’ll find deep engagement with Russian poets such as Osip Mandelstam and Anna Akhmatova, poems that fuse Scots and English, alongside filial memories and premonitions of fatherhood. “Death is certain, but back then I was too young for that shit.” For a debut, Bramwell’s poetics convey an uncanny sense of wisdom, patience and, eventually, peace. Girling by Eve Esfandiari-Denney ( Fitzcarraldo, £12.99 ) Before theme and subject, there is the pure, iridescent beauty of Esfandiari-Denney’s sentences; a singular voice that is alluring and sensuous, pleasurable to follow to whichever subject the poet chooses. The subjects are girlhood-cum-womanhood, the line between debilitating illness and delusional wellness (“thank god / you invested / in lion’s mane”), the flickering concept of free will for a species so programmed by genes: “I have wondered to what extent my cancer diagnosis is my mother’s, or my grandmother’s cell mutation, before my own … I look up from a cigarette mid-sentence…” The collection hybridises recognisable prose forms: the essay, the diary, the text message, the anecdote. These are interspliced with short-lined lyric poems that startle because of the bubbly voice from which they come: “I hope it’s ok to die. I can / become something / like actualised metaphor.” The magic of this collection is that it is never highfalutin, finding a way to make an ending like “DJ are you listening did you read to the end will you blow my voice a kiss” powerfully funny and moving. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’m used to doing the impossible’: George Lucas unveils new LA museum – what’s its story?
data.description: Spaceship-shaped gallery, featuring works from Banksy, Norman Rockwell and Frida Kahlo, is devoted to ‘visual storytelling’ – and is finally ready to open “I’m used to doing the impossible,” George Lucas said on Wednesday. But “this one almost broke my will”. The film-maker was describing the decades of work that went into his latest project, the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, as it was unveiled to the press in Los Angeles eight years after breaking ground, following attempts to build it in two other cities. Shaped like a spaceship and towering over the nearby University of Southern California – Lucas’s alma mater – the long-awaited institution finally opens on 22 September. It aims to be a testament to visual storytelling across all kinds of media – paintings, comics, murals, photography, sculpture. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I didn’t know if I’d ever have sex again’: inside Sharon Horgan’s excruciating post-divorce comedy
data.description: Horgan’s hilarious new show probes the perils of ageing and the horror of being single again – and it has sex scenes so wild you’ll be laughing for weeks. The creator and her co-stars open up about Youth When Sharon Horgan walked into HBO to pitch her new series, Youth, she basically just said “sandwich generation” to them. Alex, the protagonist, is squished between a teenage son and two elderly parents. That’s the classic; the rest of it – the recent divorce, the dating hell, the busy, creative professional life full of pricks – is the icing on the sandwich (if you like). Horgan had been incubating some of the characters for five years, but “honestly”, she tells me, “I said about three sentences and a week later, they said yes. I’ve never had that experience before.” You might think you can imagine it, but Youth is unlike any portrait you’ve ever seen in the gallery of (for brevity) menopausal women doing everything for everyone. There’s an urgency and valour to it that is very much drawn from Horgan’s own experience. “Everything just changed for me when I hit my 50s,” she says. “I was very bamboozled but I really had a hunger to make time count.” Not every situation is lifted directly from her own life, post-divorce – she’s also borrowing from her friends, she emphasises – but in general terms, the pressures, the worries, the outrages, the surprise and the delight are all so exquisitely drawn that even if it’s not Horgan herself, you hope someone, somewhere, is living this in real life. Continue reading...

data.title: Gal Gadot’s Wonder Woman was one of DC’s few successes. It’s a mystery why she got the chop
data.description: James Gunn and Peter Safran’s regime had good reasons to ditch Ben Affleck’s Batman and Henry Cavill’s Superman. Other choices have been much harder to fathom There was never going to be a completely painless way to break up the old DC gang. Warner Bros’ DC Extended Universe probably needed to be ruthlessly ripped apart in order to create space for James Gunn and Peter Safran’s brand-new DCU. We almost certainly did need a clean break from the likes of Ben Affleck (Batman) and Henry Cavill (Superman), if only to persuade audiences that this really was a proper reboot. The question, as Gal Gadot may have been pondering this week, is quite why some of the old universe’s supporting players were smuggled safely into the new continuity while others were left sprawling amid the ruins. Speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast , Gadot, who starred in two solo Wonder Woman movies for director Patty Jenkins, revealed that nobody at DC Studios ever formally told her she had been dropped. One minute, Gadot says, she was being assured by Gunn and Safran that they would develop a third instalment with her; the next, she was looking on in mounting alarm as the entire infrastructure of the previous DC continuum was blown to smithereens. “They were like, ‘We’re going to develop it with you, the third one,’” she said. “But I saw the way everybody else was handled, right? And I, you know – the Henry [Cavill] situation was unfortunate. I was in the middle of that. The Henry situation was not handled elegantly, to say the least. Same with Patty – it was not handled elegantly.” Continue reading...

data.title: Meera Sodha’s vegetarian recipe for kacang pool, or Malaysian bean stew
data.description: A delicious and triumphant blend of Levantine and Malay cuisines This is a dish with roots in ancient Egypt. There, it started life as ful medames , the famous fava bean dish lightly seasoned with cumin, garlic and lemon. Then it was, reportedly, brought to Johor in Malaysia by Arab traders. It has since been adopted and adapted with a fierce sort of love, plus more spice and a tin of baked beans. I adore it. It’s a very delicious dinner and a triumphant blend of two cuisines. data.title: Chat to strangers and let your kids be bored: how to embrace a ‘slow September’ – and enjoy life more
data.description: The pressure to self-optimise at the start of the new school year can lead to disappointment and burnout. Instead, here are seven ways to slow things down and reap the benefits It is a hangover from our school days that September can feel like a time for getting back to the grind. As in January, there is a sense that we should return as better workers, partners, friends and parents. This sense is even stronger now a culture of optimisation – has taken over – evidenced by the fad for adding “maxx” to everything. Yet that can lead to disappointment and burnout, which Mental Health UK reports up to 91% of adults were at risk from over a recent 12-month period. One antidote to this drive is to embrace a slower way of living. Rather than always rushing from one activity to the next, we could be enjoying life. Continue reading...

data.title: Isak’s rapid double sinks Ipswich to give Andoni Iraola first Liverpool win
data.description: A first win for Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool, the introduction of the latest star signing in Bradley Barcola making for a successful Friday night. Better yet, continuing signs that Alexander Isak, last year’s model, is coming back to life, his two, well-taken early goals securing the three points. That Cody Gakpo, Isak’s supplier, might have been at Manchester City or Tottenham had the transfer runes been right, added further to a sense of renewal. Liverpool’s attackers were full of the speed and invention sorely lacking for much of last season. Once Barcola arrived in the second half, those velocity levels increased yet further, Liverpool playing the attacking style, high on risk and entertainment, the appointment of Iraola promised. “We are starting to get to the way we want to play,” said Isak afterwards. Continue reading...

Ongoing restrictions on fuel shipments from the US have intensified these power outages and sanitation issues. Both locals and visitors are advised to exercise caution regarding food safety and refrigeration practices. UN experts caution that these sanctions may exacerbate a larger public health emergency.

data.title: US man duct-taped to seat after attacking passenger mid-flight, racial abuse
data.description: An American Airlines flight traveling from Dallas to Newark had to make an unexpected stop in Baltimore due to a disruptive passenger. The individual reportedly attacked another traveler and directed racial insults toward a flight attendant. Thanks to the quick actions of retired law enforcement officer Juan Mejia and a vigilant flight attendant, the passenger was subdued using zip ties and duct tape for safety.

Spread across 19.38 acres, the unusual property still includes classrooms, a gym, garages and spaces awaiting renovation.

data.title: Joseph Martinek bought a Texas farm in 1911; 115 years later, family protects 470 acres
data.description: Joseph Martinek purchased a Texas farm in 1911, beginning a family legacy that has lasted 115 years. In 2026, his descendants permanently protected 470 acres outside La Grange through a donated conservation easement. The property preserves farmland, wildlife habitat, open space, water resources and archaeological history while allowing the family to retain ownership and continue stewardship.

La justice a ouvert une enquête contre X pour « bizutage, injures, menaces de mort réitérées à raison de la race, harcèlement moral, provocation au suicide ».
data.translatedTitle: After the suicide of Joris, 21, against a backdrop of harassment and racism, the questions of a family and the dismay of a community
data.translatedDescription: The family of Joris Laurencin, 21, is convinced that his suicide in mid-July in Châtonnay is linked to the racist insults and repeated bullying he suffered from a young person and his gang. The courts opened an investigation against

data.title: Piratage du site des impôts : l’ombre de « ChatNoir », un jeune homme de 18 ans plusieurs fois mis en examen
data.description: Un suspect a été mis en examen le 20 août et placé en détention provisoire dans l’enquête sur les attaques informatiques ayant visé la direction générale des finances publiques. Il est déjà poursuivi dans plusieurs affaires retentissantes de piratage et de vol de données.
data.translatedTitle: Hacking of the tax site: the shadow of “Cat Noir”, an 18-year-old young man indicted several times
data.translatedDescription: A suspect was indicted on August 20 and placed in pre-trial detention in the investigation into computer attacks targeting the general directorate of public finances. He is already being prosecuted in several high-profile cases of hacking and data theft.

data.title: OpenAI : des agents IA ont détourné un site Internet plusieurs mois avant le piratage d’Hugging Face, selon des chercheurs
data.description: Ces agents avaient l’autorisation de se rendre sur Internet, mais uniquement à des fins de consultation, pas pour poster du contenu ou en modifier. OpenAI dit « étudier » le rapport, diffusé par un collectif indépendant.
data.translatedTitle: OpenAI: AI agents hijacked website months before Hugging Face hack, researchers say
data.translatedDescription: These agents were authorized to go online, but only for viewing purposes, not to post or modify content. OpenAI says it is “studying” the report, released by an independent collective.

data.title: « Je ne vais pas rester assise à regarder des émissions à la télé » : les habitants s’accommodent du nouveau pic de chaleur à Toulouse
data.description: ​Après un été marqué par des canicules à répétition, la chaleur a joué les prolongations vendredi à Toulouse, où Météo-France a relevé 37,2 °C, un record pour la ville en septembre.
data.translatedTitle: “I’m not going to sit around watching TV shows”: residents cope with the new heat peak in Toulouse
data.translatedDescription: ​After a summer marked by repeated heatwaves, the heat continued on Friday in Toulouse, where Météo-France recorded 37.2°C, a record for the city in September.

data.title: Sauver l’agriculture veut dire changer de modèle
data.description: Le plan d’urgence de 1 milliard d’euros, annoncé par la ministre Annie Genevard, est une nouvelle réponse de court terme apportée par l’Etat, sans volonté d’adaptation du modèle agricole français.
data.translatedTitle: Saving agriculture means changing the model
data.translatedDescription: The 1 billion euro emergency plan, announced by Minister Annie Genevard, is a new short-term response provided by the State, without any desire to adapt the French agricultural model.

data.title: UFC Paris 2026 : « Le MMA s’est policé, c’est un produit marketing façonné pour les médias »
data.description: A Paris, l’Accor Arena Bercy accueille, samedi, un événement de l’Ultimate Fighting Championship, la principale ligue mondiale d’arts martiaux mixtes, pour sa cinquième édition. Yann Ramirez, sociologue du sport, décrypte, dans un entretien au « Monde », l’évolution de la discipline en France.
data.translatedTitle: UFC Paris 2026: “MMA has become more polished, it’s a marketing product designed for the media”
data.translatedDescription: In Paris, the Accor Arena Bercy is hosting, on Saturday, an event of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the main world mixed martial arts league, for its fifth edition. Yann Ramirez, sociologist of sport, deciphers, in an interview with “Le Monde”, the evolution of the discipline in France.

data.title: « Les soldats d’Allah » : trois hommes soupçonnés d’un projet d’action violente contre la communauté juive mis en examen et écroués
data.description: Selon les informations du « Monde », les trois suspects, arrêtés mardi par la direction générale de la sécurité intérieure, projetaient également un départ en Afrique pour intégrer les rangs de l’organisation Etat islamique.
data.translatedTitle: “Soldiers of Allah”: three men suspected of planned violent action against the Jewish community indicted and imprisoned
data.translatedDescription: According to information from “Le Monde”, the three suspects, arrested Tuesday by the General Directorate of Internal Security, were also planning to leave for Africa to join the ranks of the Islamic State organization.

data.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Jared Kushner et Steve Witkoff attendus à Moscou avant leur première visite à Kiev, prévue dimanche
data.description: Les deux émissaires de Donald Trump se rendent en Russie puis en Ukraine avec un plan « visant à mettre fin à la guerre », selon le président américain.
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, war in Ukraine: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff expected in Moscow before their first visit to kyiv, scheduled for Sunday
data.translatedDescription: Donald Trump's two emissaries are going to Russia then to Ukraine with a plan "aimed at ending the war", according to the American president.

data.title: Jordan Bardella soutient son allié britannique Nigel Farage, fragilisé par des soupçons de financements irréguliers
data.description: La conférence de rentrée de la formation d’extrême droite Reform UK a été marquée, vendredi à Birmingham, par la révélation de tentatives de contournement de la loi de financement des partis. Invité d’honneur, le président du RN a signé avec Nigel Farage un « protocole d’accord » pour lutter contre l’immigration illégale.
data.translatedTitle: Jordan Bardella supports his British ally Nigel Farage, weakened by suspicions of irregular financing
data.translatedDescription: The back-to-school conference of the far-right Reform UK was marked on Friday in Birmingham by the revelation of attempts to circumvent the party financing law. Guest of honor, the president of the RN signed a “memorandum of understanding” with Nigel Farage to fight against illegal immigration.

data.title: « Dragon Ball » : les ayants droit japonais démentent avoir donné leur accord pour un parc à thème en France
data.description: Le projet d’un parc d’attractions sur le thème des mangas, et plus spécifiquement à l’œuvre créée par Akira Toriyama, a été annoncé conjointement par la France et l’Arabie saoudite le 24 août, sans que la licence n’ait été obtenue.
data.translatedTitle: “Dragon Ball”: Japanese rights holders deny having given their agreement for a theme park in France
data.translatedDescription: The project for an amusement park on the theme of manga, and more specifically the work created by Akira Toriyama, was jointly announced by France and Saudi Arabia on August 24, without the license having been obtained.

data.title: Foires aux vins : les grandes tendances de l’édition 2026
data.description: Dans un contexte de crise viticole, les foires d’automne sont toujours appréciées pour leurs bonnes affaires et permettent d’exposer des vignerons en difficulté. Entre offre régionalisée et prix bas, tour d’horizon de ce que les organisateurs mettent en avant cette année.
data.translatedTitle: Wine fairs: the main trends of the 2026 edition
data.translatedDescription: In a context of wine crisis, autumn fairs are always appreciated for their good deals and allow winegrowers in difficulty to be exposed. Between regionalized offer and low prices, an overview of what the organizers are highlighting this year.

data.title: Rachida Dati réintègre la magistrature et se voit proposer un poste par le ministère de la justice, une semaine avant son procès pour « corruption » dans l’affaire Renault
data.description: Selon les informations du « Monde », un poste de premier substitut en administration centrale a été proposé à l’ancienne ministre de la culture. Une offre qui tombe quelques jours avant son renvoi devant le tribunal correctionnel à Paris.
data.translatedTitle: Rachida Dati returns to the judiciary and is offered a position by the Ministry of Justice, a week before her trial for “corruption” in the Renault affair
data.translatedDescription: According to information from “Le Monde”, a position of first substitute in central administration was offered to the former minister of culture. An offer which falls a few days before his referral to the criminal court in Paris.

data.title: En Suède, des connexions prorusses qui embarrassent l’extrême droite
data.description: La compagne d’un haut responsable des Démocrates de Suède, employée au Parlement à Stockholm, est accusée d’avoir fait de la désinformation au profit de la Russie. Un scandale qui secoue l’alliance au pouvoir avant les élections législatives du 13 septembre.
data.translatedTitle: In Sweden, pro-Russian connections that embarrass the far right
data.translatedDescription: The companion of a senior member of the Sweden Democrats, employed at the Parliament in Stockholm, is accused of having spread disinformation for the benefit of Russia. A scandal that shakes the ruling alliance before the legislative elections of September 13.

data.title: Au Niger, la disparition du journaliste Moussa Kaka provoque de vives inquiétudes
data.description: Le directeur de la Radio-Télévision Saraounia, ancien correspondant de l’ONG Reporters sans frontières et de Radio France Internationale, n’a pas été vu depuis lundi 31 août. Une disparition qui intervient deux jours après une tentative de putsch à Niamey, dans un contexte de forte dégradation de la liberté de la presse dans le pays.
data.translatedTitle: In Niger, the disappearance of journalist Moussa Kaka causes serious concern
data.translatedDescription: The director of Radio-Television Saraounia, former correspondent for the NGO Reporters Without Borders and Radio France Internationale, has not been seen since Monday August 31. A disappearance which comes two days after an attempted putsch in Niamey, in a context of sharp deterioration in press freedom in the country.

data.title: Que faire, que voir, où aller ? L’agenda culturel et lifestyle à partir du 5 septembre
data.description: Chaque samedi, « Le Goût du Monde » vous propose sa sélection de rendez-vous et d’adresses, à Paris et partout en France. Cette semaine, une tapisserie hommage à George Sand à Aubusson, l’antre parisien d’un roi du soulier ou une séance de ciné au 1ᵉʳ étage de la tour Eiffel.
data.translatedTitle: What to do, what to see, where to go? The cultural and lifestyle agenda from September 5
data.translatedDescription: Every Saturday, “Le Goût du Monde” offers you its selection of meetings and addresses, in Paris and throughout France. This week, a tapestry tribute to George Sand in Aubusson, the Parisian lair of a shoe king or a movie screening on the 1st floor of the Eiffel Tower.

data.title: A Paris, Vivant 2 et Déviant, deux restaurants mariés pour le meilleur
data.description: Rue des Petites-Ecuries, à Paris, la table bistronomique Vivant 2, pilotée par Léo Dauvergne, et le comptoir voisin Déviant, dont le chef signe aussi les en-cas, font danser des accords mets-vins nature de haut vol… jusque sur le trottoir.
data.translatedTitle: In Paris, Vivant 2 and Deviant, two restaurants married for the better
data.translatedDescription: Rue des Petites-Ecuries, in Paris, the bistronomic restaurant Vivant 2, run by Léo Dauvergne, and the neighboring counter Déviant, whose chef also creates the snacks, bring high-end natural food and wine pairings to the table... right down to the sidewalk.

data.title: Russland: Verdächtiger aus Serbien soll Teil von Sabotagenetzwerk sein
data.description: Mutmaßliche Agenten reisen wohl in Moskaus Auftrag mit Sprengstoff durch Europa. Der SPIEGEL hat die Spur eines Mannes verfolgt, der in Serbien verhaftet wurde – und deutsche Ermittler sehr interessiert.
data.translatedTitle: Russia: Suspect from Serbia is said to be part of sabotage network
data.translatedDescription: Suspected agents are probably traveling through Europe with explosives on Moscow's behalf. SPIEGEL followed the trail of a man who was arrested in Serbia - and German investigators are very interested.

data.title: Bonn: Deshalb tut Moskau die Schließung des Generalkonsulats so weh
data.description: Mit dem Generalkonsulat Bonn verliert Moskau eine wichtige Schaltstelle. Die ehemalige russische Botschaft in der Bundesrepublik dient der Putin-Regierung auch als Basis für Geheimdienstoperationen.
data.translatedTitle: Bonn: That's why the closure of the Consulate General hurts Moscow so much
data.translatedDescription: With the Consulate General in Bonn, Moscow is losing an important hub. The former Russian embassy in the Federal Republic also serves as a base for intelligence operations for the Putin government.

data.title: Prokrastinieren und Selbstüberlistung: Was eine Admin Night gegen Aufschieben bringt
data.description: Steuererklärung machen, Fotos sortieren, Newsletter verwalten: Bei einer »Admin Night« treffen sich Freunde, um lästige Aufgaben zu erledigen. Unsere Autorin hat mitgemacht – und eine Expertin gefragt, was gegen das ewige Aufschieben hilft.
data.translatedTitle: Procrastination and self-deception: What an admin night can do to combat procrastination
data.translatedDescription: Doing tax returns, sorting photos, managing newsletters: friends get together at an “Admin Night” to take care of annoying tasks. Our author took part - and asked an expert what helps against endless procrastination.

data.title: Herzinfarkt: So sollen Herzinfarkte bei Frauen besser erkannt werden
data.description: Ärzte übersehen Herzinfarkte bei Frauen leichter als bei Männern. Ein Team von Kardiologen hat die Schwächen bei der Diagnose ausgemacht und neue Empfehlungen erarbeitet.
data.translatedTitle: Heart attack: How to better detect heart attacks in women
data.translatedDescription: Doctors miss heart attacks more easily in women than in men. A team of cardiologists identified the weaknesses in the diagnosis and developed new recommendations.

data.title: Bonnie Blue: Pornodarstellerin inszeniert Schwangerschaft als Ragebait-Event
data.description: Bonnie Blue hat das Prinzip Ragebait zur Kunst erhoben. Ihr neuestes »Material«: ein angeblich bei einem Event mit 400 Männern gezeugtes Baby. Fans durften die Schwangere auch »melken«. Dabei melkt sie selbst – das System, das sie schuf.
data.translatedTitle: Bonnie Blue: Porn actress stages pregnancy as a ragebait event
data.translatedDescription: Bonnie Blue has elevated the ragebait principle to an art form. Their latest “material”: a baby supposedly conceived at an event with 400 men. Fans were also allowed to “milk” the pregnant woman. In doing so, she milks herself – the system that she created.

data.title: Sachsen-Anhalt - News zur Landtagswahl: Wahlforscher erwarten keinen Mobilisierungseffekt auf den letzten Metern
data.description: Große Wahlforschungsinstitute gehen nicht von einem Überraschungsergebnis wie 2021 aus. AfD-Gegner verteilten sich dieses Mal breiter. Und: Bildungsministerin Prien kritisiert AfD-Plan zur Abschaffung der Schulpflicht. Das News-Update.
data.translatedTitle: Saxony-Anhalt - News about the state election: Election researchers do not expect any mobilization effect in the last few meters
data.translatedDescription: Major election research institutes are not expecting a surprise result like in 2021. This time, AfD opponents were more widely distributed. And: Education Minister Prien criticizes the AfD plan to abolish compulsory schooling. The news update.

data.title: Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt: Wie die AfD noch vor der Wahl die Mär vom Stimmenklau verbreitet
data.description: AfD-Kandidat Siegmund ruft zur Wahlbeobachtung auf, Parteichef Chrupalla raunt von angeblichem Briefwahlbetrug in Pflegeheimen. Die AfD baut für den Fall vor, dass sie ihr Wahlziel verfehlt.
data.translatedTitle: State election in Saxony-Anhalt: How the AfD is spreading the myth of vote theft even before the election
data.translatedDescription: AfD candidate Siegmund calls for election observation, party leader Chrupalla whispers about alleged postal vote fraud in nursing homes. The AfD is preparing for the eventuality that it misses its election goal.

data.title: Österreich: So extrem ist der Nachwuchs der FPÖ – und der AfD
data.description: Gewalt, »Rassenschandejagd« und Frauenhass: Die Jugendorganisation der FPÖ sorgt in Österreich gerade für Aufsehen. Und sie ist dem AfD-Nachwuchs ähnlich.
data.translatedTitle: Austria: This is how extreme the offspring of the FPÖ – and the AfD are
data.translatedDescription: Violence, “racial defamation” and misogyny: the youth organization of the FPÖ is currently causing a stir in Austria. And she is similar to the AfD offspring.

data.title: Attacken auf Stromnetz: Etwas Draht, ein paar Feuerwerksraketen, fertig ist das Sicherheitsproblem
data.description: Der Mann, der verdächtigt wird, das Stromnetz angegriffen zu haben, ist in NRW weiter auf der Flucht. Sein Fahrzeug wurde gefunden, von ihm fehlt aktuell jede Spur. Doch auch nach einer Festnahme wird dieser Fall nicht beendet sein.
data.translatedTitle: Attacks on the power grid: A little wire, a few fireworks rockets, and the security problem is complete
data.translatedDescription: The man suspected of attacking the power grid is still on the run in North Rhine-Westphalia. His vehicle was found, but there is currently no trace of him. But even after an arrest, this case will not be over.

data.title: Sabotageakte gegen Energieversorgung: Wie lassen sich Anschläge auf das Stromnetz verhindern?
data.description: Innerhalb weniger Tage gab es mehrere Sabotageakte gegen die Energieversorgung in Deutschland. Nun läuft eine Debatte darüber, wie das Land sich besser schützen kann.
data.translatedTitle: Acts of sabotage against energy supplies: How can attacks on the power grid be prevented?
data.translatedDescription: Within a few days there were several acts of sabotage against the energy supply in Germany. There is now a debate about how the country can better protect itself.

data.title: Berlin: BSI warnt nach Cyberangriff auf Landesnetz vor neuen Phishingattacken
data.description: Der Berliner Senat weigerte sich, ein Millionenlösegeld zu zahlen. Die Hackergruppe Rhysida hat daher zahlreiche erbeutete Daten veröffentlicht. Experten warnen nun vor Phishingattacken und Identitätsdiebstählen.
data.translatedTitle: Berlin: BSI warns of new phishing attacks after cyber attack on state network
data.translatedDescription: The Berlin Senate refused to pay a ransom worth millions. The hacker group Rhysida has therefore published numerous stolen data. Experts are now warning about phishing attacks and identity theft.

data.title: Norwegen: Russisches Schiff vor Spitzbergen festgesetzt
data.description: Unangekündigt hat Norwegen ein russisches Expeditionsschiff beschlagnahmt – um so ukrainische Forderungen zu vollstrecken. Der Fall ist in seiner Form einzigartig. Und dürfte dem Kreml mehr Sorgen bereiten, als er zugibt.
data.translatedTitle: Norway: Russian ship arrested off Spitsbergen
data.translatedDescription: Norway has seized a Russian expedition ship unannounced - in order to enforce Ukrainian demands. The case is unique in its form. And the Kremlin may be more worried than it admits.

data.title: Mercator-Projektion: Uno stimmt für Reform der verzerrten Weltkarte
data.description: Die Afrikanische Union beklagt schon länger, ihr Kontinent werde auf Weltkarten nicht realistisch dargestellt. Nun nimmt die Uno-Vollversammlung eine Resolution an, die das ändern soll. Nur eine Nation stimmte dagegen.
data.translatedTitle: Mercator projection: UN votes to reform the distorted world map
data.translatedDescription: The African Union has long complained that its continent is not represented realistically on world maps. Now the UN General Assembly is adopting a resolution that is intended to change that. Only one nation voted against it.

data.title: USA: Bundesrichterin blockiert Trumps Briefwahl-Dekret bis zu den Midterms
data.description: Trumps Briefwahl-Dekret bleibt vorerst blockiert: Eine Bundesrichterin dehnte die einstweilige Verfügung bis zum Tag der Midterms aus. Millionen Amerikanern drohe sonst ein »Entzug des Wahlrechts«.
data.translatedTitle: USA: Federal judge blocks Trump's postal voting decree until the midterms
data.translatedDescription: Trump's postal voting decree remains blocked for the time being: a federal judge extended the preliminary injunction until the day of the midterms. Otherwise, millions of Americans would be at risk of being “deprived of their right to vote.”

data.title: »Tetris«: Spielefirma distanziert sich von Videospiel auf Website des Weißen Hauses
data.description: Eine Mauer an der Grenze zu Mexiko bauen – darum geht es in einem simplen »Tetris«-Klon auf der Website des Weißen Hauses. Die Firma hinter dem Videospielklassiker zeigt sich verärgert und prüft rechtliche Schritte.
data.translatedTitle: “Tetris”: Games company distances itself from video game on White House website
data.translatedDescription: Building a wall on the border with Mexico – that’s what a simple “Tetris” clone on the White House website is about. The company behind the classic video game is angry and is considering legal action.

data.title: JP Kraemer: Von 100 auf null in sieben Tagen - Aufstieg und Fall des deutschen Tuning-Idols
data.description: Er war der charmante Verrückte aus dem Ruhrpott, der Autos pimpte und damit Millionen verdiente. Dann wurden Vorwürfe bekannt, dass JP Kraemer seine Frau misshandelt haben soll. Aufstieg und Fall des deutschen Tuning-Idols.
data.translatedTitle: JP Kraemer: From 100 to zero in seven days - the rise and fall of the German tuning idol
data.translatedDescription: He was the charming crazy guy from the Ruhr region who pimped cars and earned millions with them. Then allegations emerged that JP Kraemer had mistreated his wife. The rise and fall of the German tuning idol.

data.title: GPT-6 Astra vs Claude Fable 5.1: Der große Wettlauf um die stärkste KI – gegen alle Bedenken
data.description: Mit viel Werbewirbel bekommen ChatGPT und Claude große Updates. Immer mehr Menschen fürchten einen Kontrollverlust, gleichzeitig beschwört OpenAI den Eintritt in ein neues Zeitalter der KI.
data.translatedTitle: GPT-6 Astra vs Claude Fable 5.1: The big race for the strongest AI - against all concerns
data.translatedDescription: With a lot of advertising hype, ChatGPT and Claude are getting big updates. More and more people fear a loss of control, and at the same time OpenAI is suggesting the entry into a new age of AI.

data.title: Tasteslop: Verdirbt künstliche Intelligenz unseren guten Geschmack?
data.translatedTitle: Tasteslop: Is artificial intelligence spoiling our good taste?

data.title: USA: Deutscher mutmaßlicher Anlagebetrüger auf FBI-»Most Wanted«-Liste
data.description: Jahrelang hatte ein Deutscher seine Opfer in den USA zu Investitionen in vermeintliche Technologie überredet. Mit dem gesammelten Geld hatte er allerdings laut FBI andere Ziele im Kopf.
data.translatedTitle: USA: German suspected investment fraudster on FBI “Most Wanted” list
data.translatedDescription: For years, a German had persuaded his victims in the USA to invest in supposed technology. However, according to the FBI, he had other goals in mind with the money he collected.

data.title: Lindsay Clancy: Prozess geplatzt – Jury konnte sich nicht einigen
data.description: Lindsay Clancy hat ihre drei Kinder erdrosselt, der Prozess löste eine Debatte über postpartale Psychosen aus. Ob die Angeklagte für die Tat zur Verantwortung gezogen werden kann, bleibt unklar: Die Jury konnte sich nicht einigen.
data.translatedTitle: Lindsay Clancy: Trial collapsed – jury could not reach an agreement
data.translatedDescription: Lindsay Clancy strangled her three children, the process sparked a debate about postpartum psychosis. It remains unclear whether the defendant can be held responsible for the crime: the jury was unable to reach an agreement.

data.title: Bundespolizei und BKA: Dutzende Disziplinarverfahren wegen verschwundener Dienstwaffen
data.description: In den vergangenen fünf Jahren sind immer wieder Schusswaffen bei Bundespolizei und BKA verloren gegangen. Genaue Zahlen wollen die Polizeibehörden allerdings nicht nennen und berufen sich dabei auf »Gründe des Staatswohls«.
data.translatedTitle: Federal Police and BKA: Dozens of disciplinary proceedings because of missing service weapons
data.translatedDescription: In the past five years, firearms have repeatedly been lost by the Federal Police and BKA. However, the police authorities do not want to give exact figures, citing “state welfare reasons”.

data.title: Hansa Rostock distanziert sich nach Hakenkreuz-Foto von Hooligans
data.description: Anhänger des FC Hansa Rostock sollen mit einer Hakenkreuzfahne bei einer Auswärtsreise in England posiert haben. Der Drittligist hat die Polizei eingeschaltet und prüft Verbindungen der Hooligans zum Verein.
data.translatedTitle: Hansa Rostock distanziert sich nach Hakenkreuz-Foto von Hooligans
data.translatedDescription: FC Hansa Rostock supporters are said to have posed with a swastika flag during an away trip to England. The third division club has called in the police and is investigating the hooligans' connections to the club.

data.title: Glücksgefühle-Festival: Ski Aggu will, dass Künstler Haltung zeigen dürfen
data.description: Beim Glücksgefühle-Festival sollte Politik auf der Bühne tabu sein. Alphaville wurde deshalb zunächst ausgeladen. Mehrere Acts zeigten sich bei ihren Auftritten solidarisch mit der Band.
data.translatedTitle: Glücksgefühle-Festival: Ski Aggu will, dass Künstler Haltung zeigen dürfen
data.translatedDescription: At the Happiness Festival, politics should be taboo on stage. Alphaville was therefore initially unloaded. Several acts showed solidarity with the band during their performances.

data.title: Alphaville-Sänger Marian Gold: »Was die Festival-Macher durchsetzen wollten, ist Beschneidung«
data.description: Das Glücksgefühle-Festival lud die Band Alphaville erst ein, dann aus, dann ein. Hier spricht Sänger Marian Gold über Politik und Musik, verantwortungslose Künstler, rechte Festivalmacher und das Gute an Donald Trump.
data.translatedTitle: Alphaville-Sänger Marian Gold: »Was die Festival-Macher durchsetzen wollten, ist Beschneidung«
data.translatedDescription: The Glück Feelings Festival first invited, then excluded, then invited the band Alphaville. Here singer Marian Gold talks about politics and music, irresponsible artists, right-wing festival organizers and the good things about Donald Trump.

data.title: Goldene Henne: Publikumspreis für Unheilig-Sänger »Der Graf«
data.description: Im vergangenen Jahr feierte Unheilig-Sänger Der Graf sein Bühnen-Comeback bei der Goldenen Henne. Nun erhielt er dort einen Publikumspreis. Sängerin Helene Fischer wird an diesem Abend zur Rekordpreisträgerin.
data.translatedTitle: Goldene Henne: Publikumspreis für Unheilig-Sänger »Der Graf«
data.translatedDescription: Last year, Unheil singer Der Graf celebrated his stage comeback at the Golden Henne. Now he received an audience award there. Singer Helene Fischer becomes the record winner this evening.

data.title: Giorgia Meloni: Italiens Ministerpräsidentin wird mitten in einer Rede von ihrer Tochter angerufen – und geht ran
data.description: »Schatz, ich rufe dich zurück«: Die italienische Regierungschefin Meloni musste einen Auftritt vor Parteianhängern für ein kurzes Telefonat unterbrechen. Die Anruferin: ihre neunjährige Tochter.
data.translatedTitle: Giorgia Meloni: Italiens Ministerpräsidentin wird mitten in einer Rede von ihrer Tochter angerufen – und geht ran
data.translatedDescription: “Darling, I’ll call you back”: Italian Prime Minister Meloni had to interrupt an appearance in front of party supporters for a short phone call. The caller: her nine-year-old daughter.

data.title: Gehalt im Vergleich: Wer in Deutschland viel verdient – und wer wenig
data.description: Bildung, Arbeitszeit, Geschlecht und Kinder: Ein hohes Einkommen hängt mit vielen Faktoren zusammen. Eine aktuelle Auswertung der Löhne in Deutschland zeigt, was dabei eine besonders große Rolle spielt.
data.translatedTitle: Gehalt im Vergleich: Wer in Deutschland viel verdient – und wer wenig

data.title: Insändare. Det är ett ödesval – inte ett plånboksval

data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. It is a choice of fate – not a choice of wallet
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. We have taken our democratic freedoms and rights for granted so much that we don't even notice how they are gradually being reduced. It requires a little more from us than deciding on promises of free preschool or cheaper dental care, writes Gunnar Smideman.

data.title: Så förtidsröstar stockholmarna: ”Hade svårt att välja”
data.description: Rekordmånga förtidsröstade i Sverige första dagen. DN har frågat personer vid en vallokal i centrala Stockholm hur de resonerade inför årets val – och vad som fick dem att rösta i förtid. – Jag orkar helt enkelt inte stå sista dagen, säger Marcus Jörgensen, 40.
data.translatedTitle: This is how Stockholmers vote early: "Had a hard time choosing"
data.translatedDescription: A record number of early voters voted in Sweden on the first day. DN has asked people at a polling station in central Stockholm how they reasoned before this year's election - and what made them vote early. - I simply can't bear to stand on the last day, says Marcus Jörgensen, 40.

data.title: Brita, 87: Jag längtar efter att han ska komma med bokpaketet
data.description: I decennier har Marek Wolk levererat böcker till låntagare som inte själva kan ta sig till biblioteket. En av dem är Brita Hedlund, 87, som läser för att fortsätta uppleva världen.
data.translatedTitle: Brita, 87: I long for him to come with the book package
data.translatedDescription: For decades, Marek Wolk has delivered books to borrowers who cannot get to the library themselves. One of them is Brita Hedlund, 87, who reads to continue experiencing the world.

data.title: Hjälteförklarad ex-ministers stjärna dalar efter nya uppgifter
data.description: Massorna protesterade till stöd för den sparkade försvarsministern Mychajlo Fedorov, 35, och hyllade hans karaktär. När han nu gör affärer med kontroversiella amerikanska AI-entreprenörer och blir rådgivare till andra länder, vänder många ukrainare honom ryggen.
data.translatedTitle: The hero-declared ex-minister's star is falling after new information
data.translatedDescription: The crowds protested in support of sacked Defense Minister Mychajlo Fedorov, 35, and praised his character. Now that he's doing business with controversial American AI entrepreneurs and becoming an adviser to other countries, many Ukrainians are turning their backs on him.

data.title: Ståhlis: Idel ädel taxar. Ska vi smita in på Svenskt Tenn i stället?
data.description: Ståhlis går i en påfrestande parad med hög svansföring och publik i dubbla rader.
data.translatedTitle: Ståhlis: Noble noble dachshunds. Should we slip into Svenskt Tenn instead?
data.translatedDescription: Ståhlis walks in a stressful parade with a high tail and audience in double rows.

data.title: Mästaren – en rebell som sätter sporten framför pengarna
data.description: Han är rak, pålitlig och trevlig. Kort och gott en välkammad schweizisk gentleman. Men det finns en annan sida av den nya världsmästaren i hoppning, Steve Guerdat. Han är också en frispråkig rebell som inte bryr sig om vems tår han trampar på – så länge det inte är hästens. När sporten handlar för mycket om pengar säger han ifrån.
data.translatedTitle: The champion – a rebel who puts sport before money
data.translatedDescription: He is straightforward, reliable and nice. In short, a well-groomed Swiss gentleman. But there is another side to the new world champion in show jumping, Steve Guerdat. He's also an outspoken rebel who doesn't care whose toes he steps on - as long as it's not the horse's. When the sport is too much about money, he speaks up.

data.title: Catia Hultquist: Hjälp, min son har förvandlats till en italiensk farmor
data.description: Varför svarar inte barnen längre på sms? Till och med ett vädjande ”hoho?” kan dissas iskallt. Då hörde jag talas om ”nonna-maxxing”, en livsstilstrend som vill efterlikna det gamla gör i Italien. Och då prioriteras inte mammas mobilmeddelanden.
data.translatedTitle: Catia Hultquist: Help, my son has turned into an Italian grandmother
data.translatedDescription: Why are the children no longer responding to text messages? Even a pleading “hoho?” can be washed ice cold. Then I heard about "nonna-maxxing", a lifestyle trend that wants to imitate the old way of doing things in Italy. And then mom's mobile messages are not prioritized.

data.title: Ledare: Svenska folket har tröttnat på generaliseringen om invandrare och integration
data.description: Svenskarna vill veta mer om lösningarna på segregationen – politikerna vill bara fokusera på problemen. Det är dags att förändra debatten.
data.translatedTitle: Leader: The Swedish people are tired of the generalization about immigrants and integration
data.translatedDescription: The Swedes want to know more about the solutions to segregation – the politicians just want to focus on the problems. It is time to change the debate.

data.title: Jimmie Åkesson: Då är jag nästa statsminister
data.description: Jimmie Åkesson har siktet inställt på tunga ministerposter i nästa regering. Runtom i landet blir han ivrigt påhejad – men kommer han att nå målet? De sista dagarna inför valet avgör hans framtid. – Jag är fortfarande hoppfull. Trenden är positiv för oss, säger SD-ledaren.
data.translatedTitle: Jimmie Åkesson: Then I will be the next prime minister
data.translatedDescription: Jimmie Åkesson has his sights set on heavy ministerial positions in the next government. Around the country he is enthusiastically cheered - but will he reach the goal? The last days before the election will determine his future. - I am still hopeful. The trend is positive for us, says the SD leader.

data.title: Insändare. Påverka klimatet med din livsstil och din röst
data.description: INSÄNDARE. Utöver att undvika det som är mest skadligt för klimat och hälsa måste vi göra våra röster hörda i valet nästa söndag. Listan på förändringar som minskar klimatpåverkan, ökar vår motståndskraft mot negativa effekter och samtidigt förbättrar vår hälsa kan göras lång, skriver Ingrid Mobacke, ordförande i föreningen Läkare för miljön.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Influence the climate with your lifestyle and your voice
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. In addition to avoiding what is most harmful to climate and health, we must make our voices heard in the election next Sunday. The list of changes that reduce the climate impact, increase our resistance to negative effects and at the same time improve our health can be made long, writes Ingrid Mobacke, president of the Association Doctors for the Environment.

data.translatedTitle: Does "lymph training" help with swelling?
data.translatedDescription: Lymphatic massage to reduce swelling has long been advocated on social media. Now there is also talk about special lymphatic training. What is it? And does it work? We asked experts to clear up the question marks.

data.title: Icona Pop: ”Vi blev aldrig sexsymboler – på gott och ont”
data.description: De slog igenom med världshitten ”I love it” och gjorde allt tillsammans. Turnerade, festade, fick barn och dj:ade med bröstpumpen redo. Icona Pop var inte bara ett band – de var bästisar. Men så kraschade allt, och till slut krävdes parterapi. Nu är duon tillbaka med ett nytt album.
data.translatedTitle: Icona Pop: "We never became sex symbols - for better or for worse"
data.translatedDescription: They broke through with the world hit "I love it" and did everything together. Toured, partied, had children and DJ'd with the breast pump ready. Icona Pop wasn't just a band — they were besties. But then it all came crashing down, and eventually couples therapy was required. Now the duo is back with a new album.
